claim: The EC rejected Apple's security-based justification for App Store linking restrictions, finding Apple failed to show why a developer's own website would be less secure than third-party sites.
stance_target: anti-steering restrictions are necessary/proportionate security measures rather than rent extraction
quoted_support: Apple's justification for its linking restrictions on security grounds was dismissed. The Commission found Apple failed to show why the app developer's own website would be less secure than third-party sites or why restrictions were necessary and proportionate.

claim: The Commission held that gatekeepers cannot average compliance across business terms; every set of terms must independently satisfy DMA obligations, rejecting Apple's 'cosmetic compliance' where developer disincentives (fees/technical barriers) offset the nominal choice offered.
stance_target: Apple's compliance changes constitute meaningful, durable removal of steering restrictions
quoted_support: The Commission found that Apple's user-facing choices were not genuinely meaningful or operable, as developers faced disincentives such as fees and technical barriers... Nominal or formal compliance fails to meet the DMA standard.

claim: The Apple and Meta DMA investigations concluded in approximately 13 months, a swift timeline compared to traditional EU competition proceedings, signaling sustained enforcement priority rather than a one-off action.
stance_target: regulatory exposure is an ongoing, recurring risk over a 2-5 year holding horizon, not a one-time settled cost
quoted_support: The Apple and Meta investigations took approximately 13 months — a relatively swift timeline compared to traditional competition cases — demonstrating the Commission's commitment to timely DMA enforcement.

claim: Apple is challenging the DMA's limited initial case-file access procedure under Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/814 as a potential basis for legal review, indicating ongoing legal uncertainty in DMA enforcement mechanics beyond the substantive fine.
stance_target: legal/procedural risk timeline relevant to first-instance ruling
quoted_support: Apple challenged aspects of this approach, which may become a basis for legal review.
